newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stock index falls to 1996 intraday low.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stock index falls to 1996 intraday low.

text.p: The South Korean stock index fell to a 1996 intraday low of 710.02 in mid-morning trading on Thursday on fears of national union strife protesting the government's plan to revise labour laws, brokers said.
The composite index fell 5.85 points in about the first hour's trading from Wednesday's close.
The previous intraday low was 710.49 on November 26.
"Worries about confrontation between the government and union groups are mounting. That's really bad news," said Chang Keun-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities.
On Wedensday, members of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions voted overwhelmingly to strike in protest at plans to revise labour laws that they believe threaten jobs.

The confederation said unions that voted to go on strike represented Hyundai Motor Co, South Korea's largest carmaker, Kia Motors Corp, Hyundai Heavy Industries Co and Daewoo Heavy Industries Co. It claims membership of around 500,000.
The index fell further to 708.44, down 7.43 points, by 10:36 a.m. (0136 GMT).
